title: Liber Scivias
shelf_note: A Latin manuscript of Hildegard's Scivias (Heidelberg footer: digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/salX16), so it belongs on the Latin shelf. The '1151' date is when the work was composed, not when this copy was made.
rights_flag: The scan footer carries a credit burned into the image: '© Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg' and 'gefördert von der Manfred Lautenschläger Stiftung'. This is the library's digitisation credit on a medieval manuscript, not a modern edition. The reuse licence should be checked, but this does not look like an in-copyright text.
structure_note: The book field says pages_translated is 400, but the structure count says 0. The two disagree. The leaf carries a pencilled folio number ('114') on the recto only, so a printed number shared by recto and verso, or misread, would explain much of printed_repeats 90 and printed_backsteps 32. I read these as foliation artefacts, not a scan splice.

tr_errors.source: qa recta he rednare filio amisi mada: qui cre aus filui iniusticia detaui e gla felicians
tr_errors.english: For it is right that this redeem the lost son, who was created and through injustice lost the glory of happiness.
tr_errors.problem: fluent English invented on the misreading. The source says 'because I lost the rightful inheritance of sons…', not that something rightly 'redeems the lost son'.

tr_errors.source: Hoc tale e Sicut pastor grege sui pas cet eu suum lege qua ipsemet pme plantauit.
tr_errors.english: This means: As a shepherd he will feed his flock, that is, through his law, which he himself first planted.
tr_errors.problem: this inherits the OCR omission. 'So my Son, the good shepherd, will feed his redeemed flock. How? He feeds it…' is missing, and 'through his law' is attached to the wrong subject.

tr_errors.source: Sicut pastor grege sui pascet in brachio suo leuabit suas ipse portabit.
tr_errors.english: "As a shepherd he will feed his flock; in his arm he will gather the lambs, and he himself will carry them."
tr_errors.problem: 'gather the lambs' is not in the transcription. It was restored from memory of Isaiah 40:11, while 'in sinu suo leuabit' and 'fetas' are still missing.

tr_errors.source: Istud e cunctus unus que uidet inspectore pu patris.
tr_errors.english: This is the one thing that you see in the breast of the aforesaid father.
tr_errors.problem: this follows the misreading. The image seems to name a shining light seen in the father's breast.

tr_errors.source: nisi qd acutissime uident facie patris
tr_errors.english: for they see most keenly the face of the Father

other.note: Fragments from the facing leaf are presented as marginal notes and 'translated' into a vertical list of English stubs ('the unripe / full and / in all / has in …'). A reader sees this on sight.
A raw '<column-break/>' sits in the reader text

missing.english: This is the one thing that you see in the breast of the aforesaid father.
missing.why: The sentence refers to a figure in the vision being explained. Without a note saying it explains part of the vision image, a reader cannot tell who 'the aforesaid father' is or what 'you see'.

missing.english: as Isaiah the prophet, my servant, says: "As a shepherd he will feed his flock;
missing.why: No reference (Isaiah 40:11) is given for the quotation, and the speaker 'I, the Father' is not identified as the voice of the vision.

book_verdict: The page is the right leaf of a 12th/13th-century Scivias manuscript. The main text is broadly readable in English, but the scribe's abbreviations are often misread and two passages are silently dropped, one of them the 'good shepherd' explanation. A strip of the facing leaf is shown as translated marginalia, which an expert would flag on sight.
